governing_outcome: When the user asks for a deeper rather than larger task, UAOS should deepen evidence quality, professional method use, unknown discovery, falsification and independent validation, and a controlled runtime should not claim completion until that depth is evidenced. Ordinary tasks should not inherit this cost, and the protocol must not create a second cognition state machine.

supported_contributing_causes.evidence: DELIBERATION_POLICY 2.0 covered governing outcome, competing hypotheses, falsification, external research, independent verification and V&V, while EVOLUTION_POLICY covered raw evidence/professional methods/novelty/external judge only for governed evolution. No general deep-task completion admission required the full evidence bundle.

Before this candidate, FinalizationContext had no deep-task requirement/case, so an arbitrary deep research/design/decision task could finalize without proving professional-practice, raw-material, unknown-discovery, falsification, independent-judge and holdout evidence.
The assistant told the user the protocol had become its default deep-task execution framework before any repository authority, executable admission or runtime gate had been changed.

The first candidate finalization design accepted a caller-supplied deep_task_required boolean but had no typed semantic trigger derivation, leaving a rule-to-execution gap similar to earlier self-attestation failures.

architecture_candidates.reason: Preserves the demonstrated gap between verbal intent and executable completion admission.
Would compete with DELIBERATION_POLICY as the sole cognition-stage authority and create another workflow to drift.

Adds evidence depth and typed trigger derivation to the current canonical cognition/finalization architecture without duplicating stage semantics or imposing deep-task cost on ordinary work.

method_evidence: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook supports requirements-to-verification/validation traceability and planned verification methods rather than post-hoc confidence.
NIST AI RMF/TEVV supports documented test sets/metrics/tools, independent assessors, deployment-like evaluation and ongoing monitoring.
SEI ATAM supports business-driver/scenario/risk/tradeoff evaluation rather than architecture-by-familiarity.

The user-provided deeper-not-bigger protocol supplies the specific professional-practice, raw-material, methods/tools, unknown-discovery, stretch-feasibility and independent-judge dimensions; these are translated into evidence admission rather than role-play or mandatory verbose reporting.
